data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test is installed under a fail-first ritual that creates a circular dependency: the test's expected output is defined by the guard that was written to make the test pass. The 3-of-26 result is the number of mutations that fall outside this circular closure \u2014 mutations that neither the guard nor the test was ever constructed to address. The 1-of-9 compile.py loss and the 4/4 to 6/7 spread are both explained by the same tautological structure: a test that passes by construction against its own guard cannot describe mutations outside that construction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test is shown to fail for reasons independent of the guard's condition, the circularity claim is refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3 surviving mutations are demonstrably within the guard's stated condition and still pass, the closure mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an ordinarily-guarded module shows a mutation caught by a test that was never shown failing, the circular dependency is not universal.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shown-to-fail ritual includes a re-run of all tests against all mutations after installation, the circular closure cannot cause loss.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In shown-to-fail-first installation, the sequence is: (1) plant mutation, (2) show test fails, (3) write guard, (4) test passes. Step 4 passes by construction because the guard was written to make the test pass. The test now constrains the guard but not the code \u2014 the test is a restatement of the guard's condition, not an independent description of behavior. Mutations that survive are those outside the circular closure: they are not addressed by any guard, so no test was ever shown failing for them, so no test constrains them. The 3 survivors are the residue of this circularity. The 1-of-9 compile.py loss is a mutation that fell outside the guard's construction closure and was therefore never re-tested after the guard landed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
